author: draganrakita
content: In this path, user is blind on amount of execution gas it has. But if execution gas (that is global counter now) is hit, whole tx is reverted so no changes are made.

author: gaxanh
content:
I'm not sure I fully understand your point, but under the current spec, execution gas is initialized after the intrinsic gas phase and allocated to each subframe according to EIP-150, with each subframe having its own gasleft() budget.

If we use a global execution gas counter, exhausting it would cause the entire transaction to revert rather than just the current frame. This seems like a potential DoS vector, since execution gas is currently only monotonically decreasing.

author: draganrakita
content:
This Idea is for gasLeft to be execution+state, while there is global counter for execution gas that can be hit at any time after tx have spend more than 16M of gas.

I guess halt behavior would be troublesome to support here.

It is not a dos vector as you are charging what needs to be charged

author: gaxanh
content:
> It is not a dos vector as you are charging what needs to be charged
I mean a DoS vector against the user: a malicious callee could deliberately exhaust the execution gas limit, causing the entire transaction submitted by the user to fail.

author: draganrakita
content: True, that is a attack vector. Nasty one indeed. At least all is reverted, so no changes are made.
